use_ok AnnotationSourceAdaptor: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSourceAdaptor module compiles and loads

get_all_from_cache: with the default offline test config the adaptor returns exactly one source — a Cache::Transcript whose full attribute hash matches, including dir, cache_region_size, the cache's info.txt metadata (assembly GRCh38.p5, GENCODE 24, dbSNP 149, …) and valid_chromosomes [21, 22, LRG_485]

description: file - get: the file accessor reads back the path new() stored, i.e. a custom source keeps its own source path as per-object state
file - set: file('foo/bar') both re-points the source at a new path and returns the new value, so a source can be aimed somewhere else after construction

short_name - get default: a source built with no short_name names itself after the last '/'-separated segment of its path ('foo/bar' -> 'bar'), and that name is the key its values appear under in VEP output
short_name - set: short_name('foo') overwrites the derived default and returns it, so the output key is caller-settable and not merely a function of the path
type - get default: a source built without type= matches by 'overlap', the permissive default of the four modes — so an unspecified --custom spec reports every feature touching the variant
type - set: type('exact') is accepted and returned, so a member of %VALID_TYPES passes the same check that rejects 'bar' in rows 5 and 12
type - invalid set: type('foo') on an existing source throws 'New type ... is not valid', so the closed-set check guards the setter and not only the constructor (row 5 is the constructor arm)
excerpt: throws_ok {$as->type('foo')} qr/New type .+ is not valid/, 'type - invalid set';

description: report_coords - get default: report_coords defaults to 0, so a matched feature contributes the identifier found in the source rather than the feature's own coordinates
report_coords - set: report_coords(1) flips the source to reporting coordinates and returns the new value — the toggle the --custom spec's coords= key drives

annotate_InputBuffer - overlap: annotating the 21:25585733 C/T buffer under the default overlap type attaches _custom_annotations keyed 'test.vcf.gz' - the source's default short_name, i.e. its own basename - holding the single hit { name => 'test1' }, the ID column of the overlapping VCF record and nothing else

annotate_InputBuffer - overlap - insertion: a zero-length insertion given in Ensembl start>end form (21 25585746 25585745 -/C) still finds the VCF record at 25585745 (ins2, A/AT) and is recorded as { name => 'ins2' }

annotate_InputBuffer - VCF score: with summary_stats set to ['min'], the hit on test1 gains a score field carrying the VCF QUAL column (29) alongside its name - asking for a statistic is what makes the per-record score visible at all

annotate_InputBuffer - no VCF score: the same summary_stats ['min'] request over the insertion that matches ins2, whose QUAL column is '.', yields { name => 'ins2' } with NO score key - a missing quality is dropped rather than recorded as '.' or 0

annotate_InputBuffer - overlap - no ID reports coords: with report_coords explicitly 0, a variant at 21:25585753 matching the VCF record whose ID column is '.' is recorded as { name => '21:25585753-25585753' } - the fallback is triggered by the absent ID, not by the coords flag

annotate_InputBuffer - overlap - report_coords: after report_coords(1), the same 21:25585733 variant whose matching record DOES carry the ID test1 is recorded as { name => '21:25585733-25585733' } - the flag overrides an available identifier

annotate_InputBuffer - fields: with fields(['FOO','GOO','NOVALUE']) the record gains a fields hash carrying FOO => 'BAR', the multi-value GOO re-joined as 'CAR,STAR' because overlap is not allele-aware, NOVALUE => 1 for a valueless INFO key, and FILTER => ['PASS'] which nobody asked for

annotate_InputBuffer - exact, info keyed on allele: a SECOND pass over the same buffer with type('exact'), short_name('foo') and fields(['GOO']) adds a 'foo' key holding { name => 'test1', allele => 'T', fields => { GOO => 'CAR', FILTER => ['PASS'] } } - the ALT-index-0 chunk of GOO=CAR,STAR - while the earlier 'test.vcf.gz' entry survives untouched with its full field set

annotate_InputBuffer - exact, multiple, rev strand input: an input given on the minus strand as 21:25585733 G/A/C matches BOTH ALTs of the plus-strand VCF record test1 (C to T,G) and produces TWO records under 'foo', allele 'A' with GOO 'CAR' and allele 'C' with GOO 'STAR' - the alleles reported in the input's own orientation while the INFO chunk is picked by the matched ALT index

annotate_InputBuffer - deletion: a single-base deletion 21:25585736 G/- matches two VCF records whose alleles trim down to it - del1 (ATG to A,AT, ALT index 1) with GOO 'B', and del2 (TG to T, INFO '.') with no requested field at all - and both records carry allele '-' plus their own FILTER list, del2's being the two-token ['SEGDUP','RF']

annotate_InputBuffer - mixed - insertion: with two variants of different classes in one buffer, buffer[0], the insertion 21:25585741-25585740 -/C, is annotated from ins1 (A to AC,C) as allele 'C' with GOO 'YAR' - the ALT-index-0 chunk

annotate_InputBuffer - mixed - snp: buffer[1], the substitution 21:25585740 A/C in the same buffer, is annotated from the SAME ins1 record as allele 'C' but with GOO 'ZAR' - the ALT-index-1 chunk, because here 'C' is the second ALT rather than the trimmed first

annotate_InputBuffer - trim input - insertion 1: an input written with one shared 5' base, 21:25585740 G/GC, is trimmed to the bare insertion before matching and lands on ins1 ALT 0 as allele 'C' with GOO 'YAR'
annotate_InputBuffer - trim input - insertion 2: the same insertion written with TWO shared 5' bases, 21:25585739-25585740 AG/AGC, also reduces to allele 'C' on ins1 ALT 0 with GOO 'YAR'

annotate_InputBuffer - trim input - snp 1: 21:25585740-25585741 AG/CG, one shared 3' base, matches ins1 ALT 1 - and the recorded allele is the UNtrimmed input allele 'CG', not the trimmed 'C', with GOO 'ZAR'
annotate_InputBuffer - trim input - snp 2: 21:25585740-25585742 AGT/CGT, two shared 3' bases, likewise matches ins1 ALT 1 and is recorded with the untrimmed allele 'CGT' and GOO 'ZAR'
annotate_InputBuffer - trim input - snp 3: 21:25585738-25585741 GGAG/GGCG, shared bases at BOTH ends, matches ins1 ALT 1 and is recorded with the whole untrimmed allele 'GGCG' and GOO 'ZAR'

annotate_InputBuffer - trim VCF - deletion 1: the two-base deletion 21:25585771-25585772 TT/- matches comp1 (25585770 ATTT to ATT,AT,C) once its ALT index 1 is trimmed to the same deletion, and is recorded under 'foo' as allele '-' with FOO 'CAR', the index-1 chunk of FOO=BAR,CAR,STAR

annotate_InputBuffer - trim VCF - deletion 2: the same deletion shifted one base into the T homopolymer, 21:25585772-25585773 TT/-, matches the same comp1 record with the same allele '-' and FOO 'CAR'

annotate_InputBuffer - SV reverts to overlap: a structural input parsed from VCF (21:25585735 T . with SVTYPE=DEL;SVLEN=1) is annotated through the SUPERCLASS overlap logic even though the source is still in exact mode - the record under 'foo' is { name => 'del2', fields => { FILTER => ['SEGDUP','RF'] } }, with no allele key

annotate_InputBuffer - REF included in INFO chunks: for refinc (21:25585760 C to T with FOO=0.9,0.1 - two values for one ALT), the annotation records FOO => 0.1, so the leading chunk is understood as the REF's and dropped rather than assigned to the ALT

annotate_InputBuffer - INFO chunk count doesnt match ALT count: for countwrong (21:25585761 C to T with FOO=0.7,0.2,0.1 - three values for one ALT), no per-allele assignment is attempted and the whole raw string '0.7,0.2,0.1' is recorded

annotate_InputBuffer - COSMIC id without duplication: a second source built on cosmic.vcf.gz, whose FIVE records at 1:36469721 TG/T all carry the ID COSV58963001 (one per affected transcript), annotates the matching input exactly ONCE, as { name => 'COSV58963001' } under the key 'cosmic.vcf.gz'

annotate_InputBuffer - FILTER suppression: with custom_suppress_filter set to 1 and fields ['FOO','GOO','NOVALUE'], the 21:25585733 C/T input is annotated under 'test' as allele 'T' with FOO 'BAR', GOO 'CAR' and NOVALUE 1 - and NO FILTER key at all, where n=17 and every earlier fields row got one unasked

annotate_InputBuffer - FILTER suppression off: the same source with custom_suppress_filter set back to 0, re-annotating the same variant after the previous annotations are deleted, again carries FILTER => ['PASS'] alongside the three requested INFO fields

headers - BAM_EDIT: --refseq extends the CSQ Format list with REFSEQ_MATCH, REFSEQ_OFFSET, GIVEN_REF, USED_REF and BAM_EDIT, in that order, and drops SOURCE
fields - default: the default CSQ vocabulary is the 21 core field names in a fixed order, plus whatever a --custom source contributes
fields - flag on: asking for SIFT (sift => 'b') adds a SIFT column to the CSQ vocabulary, appended after the 21 core names

fields - --merged and --custom dont duplicate SOURCE: a merged cache contributes REFSEQ_MATCH, SOURCE and REFSEQ_OFFSET contiguously, and SOURCE appears exactly once even though two features both want it
fields - user-defined: --fields Allele,Consequence replaces the whole CSQ vocabulary with the two named columns, in the user's order
output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - empty: an empty field hash still renders one empty field per vocabulary entry (20 bare pipes for 21 fields), so a consumer can index CSQ by position
output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk: one populated field renders in its own position and the remaining 20 stay empty, so a value never shifts into a neighbour's slot
output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - allele revcomped: a negative strand argument reverse-complements the Allele field only, turning A into T while every other field is left alone
output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - "-" erased: a lone hyphen in a non-Allele field is VEP's null sentinel and is written as an empty field, not as a literal -
output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - "-" intact for Allele: the Allele column is exempt from the hyphen-is-null rule, because there a - is a real allele (a deletion)
output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - ";" uri encoded: a semicolon inside a CSQ value is written %3B, because a raw one would end the INFO key and split the column
output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - "|" converted: a pipe inside a CSQ value becomes &, because a raw one would open a new field and shift every later field by one
output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - "," converted: a comma inside a CSQ value becomes &, because a raw one would end the whole consequence entry and split one transcript's annotation in two
output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - whitespace converted: a RUN of whitespace inside a CSQ value collapses to a single underscore, so 'A  G' (two spaces) is written A_G
output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - '0' kept: a field whose value is the string 0 is emitted as 0, not as an empty field
output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - 0 kept: the numeric twin of the previous row -- a field whose value is the number 0 is emitted as 0
output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - empty string provided: an explicitly empty value renders as an empty field rather than being dropped, so a two-field record is |0 and not 0

non-VCF input - deletion: an Ensembl-format deletion (C/-) becomes a VCF-legal left-anchored GC>G record, pulling the anchor base from the FASTA and shifting POS back by one
trash existing CSQ 1: an input INFO of BAR=blah;CSQ=foo;BAR2=blah2 loses only the old CSQ, keeps BAR and BAR2 in input order, and gains the new CSQ at the end
trash existing CSQ 2: the same rule with CSQ first -- CSQ=foo;BAR=blah leaves BAR=blah followed by the new CSQ, so removal does not depend on the key's position
trash existing CSQ 3: the same rule with CSQ last -- BAR=blah;CSQ=foo leaves BAR=blah followed by the new CSQ, which is where the third position closes the case
keep existing CSQ: with keep_csq set, the input's old CSQ=foo is kept alongside the new one, so the line carries two CSQ keys
dont trash BCSQ: BCSQ, the bcftools consequence key, is left alone -- only the literal CSQ key is replaced, not every key whose name ends in CSQ
vcf_info_field: with vcf_info_field => 'EFF' the annotation is written under an EFF key and the line carries no CSQ at all

no consequences added: a variant whose consequence set is empty is written with a bare . in INFO, not with an empty CSQ= key

description: use test: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser base class loads under `use` -- the format dispatcher and per-variant validation pass this whole file is about
new is defined: `Parser->new({file => test_vcf})` returns a defined object, so the base class resolved and opened the input path it was handed
check class: the object `Parser->new` returned with no `format` and no config is blessed into the base class itself rather than into one of the seven format subclasses
need config object to use new with format: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config module loads under `use`, so a config carrying `fasta` and `offline => 1` can be built for the subtests below
file: the `file` accessor reads back the input path the parser was constructed with
file STDIN: the literal string `stdin` selects *main::STDIN as the input handle, so a VEP run can sit in the middle of a shell pipe
file not exists: `$p->file('foo')` dies with /File.+does not exist/, so a parser refuses a path it cannot open instead of quietly yielding an empty variant stream
excerpt: throws_ok {$p->file('foo')} qr/File.+does not exist/, 'file not exists';

description: line_number get: a parser that has read nothing reports line 0
line_number set: assigning a line number returns it, so the counter that warning messages quote is settable as well as readable

headers: the base class's `headers` is a hard-coded empty arrayref -- `sub headers { return []; }` at Parser.pm:208-210, documented there as "Just a stub here" -- so the accessor every format subclass overrides answers [] on the base class itself
detect_format - VCF: sniffing a plain uncompressed VCF returns the format name `vcf`
gzipped VCF: `$p->file($test_gzvcf)` returns a GLOB rather than a path, i.e. a gzip-compressed VCF is opened transparently instead of being rejected or read as bytes
detect_format - gzipped VCF: sniffing sees through the gzip layer, so a compressed VCF is named `vcf` rather than treated as binary
delimiter - set: assigning a tab makes it the field separator the parser splits input lines on, and the assignment returns it
delimiter - get: the field separator reads back as the tab that was set
valid_chromosomes empty: a parser built without a chromosome list has an empty valid set, so nothing has been ruled out yet
valid_chromosomes: the constructor argument `valid_chromosomes => [21]` becomes the membership hash {21 => 1} the parser tests contigs against
minimal: `minimise_alleles` reduces GA/GT to a VariationFeature with allele_string A/T, start 2 (from 1), end 1, minimised 1 and original_allele_string GA/GT
minimal - trim both ends: `minimise_alleles` reduces GAC/GTC to A/T, i.e. it trims the shared suffix as well as the shared prefix
minimal - long trim: a 25 bp pair differing at one interior base reduces to A/T, so the both-end trim is not capped at one base per side
get_SO_term - insertion: the structural-variant type abbreviation INS maps to the SO term insertion
get_SO_term - deletion: the structural-variant type abbreviation DEL maps to the SO term deletion
get_SO_term - inversion: the structural-variant type abbreviation INV maps to the SO term inversion
get_SO_term - tandem_repeat: the structural-variant type abbreviation TREP maps to the SO term tandem_repeat
get_SO_term - chromosome_breakpoint: the structural-variant type abbreviation BND maps to the SO term chromosome_breakpoint
get_SO_term - mobile_element_deletion: the structural-variant type abbreviation DEL_ME maps to the SO term mobile_element_deletion
validate_svf - ok: a structural-variant feature whose allele string is <DEL>,<DUP> passes the SVF validation pass, which returns 1
validate_svf - skip: an SVF carrying vep_skip => 1 is rejected, so validate_svf returns 0 and the variant never reaches the caller
validate_vf - ok: a well-formed G/C VariationFeature passes the whole per-variant validation chain, which returns 1
validate_vf - create variation_name: a VariationFeature with no identifier is given the synthesised name 1_1_G/C, i.e. chr_start_ref/alt
validate_vf - chr list include: with the per-run chromosome list set to ['1'], a variant on chromosome 1 passes and returns 1
validate_vf - chr list exclude: with the same list set to ['1'], a variant on chromosome 2 is rejected and returns 0
validate_vf - uppercase allele_string: a lowercase input allele string g/c is rewritten in place to G/C before annotation
have_chr - pass: `_have_chr` returns 1 because the bare contig 1 is in the valid set, against the valid set {1, 21, CHR_1, MT, chromosome, chr12} built at perl/Parser.t:117
have_chr - remove chr: `_have_chr` returns 1 because the prefixed query chr1 matches the bare valid entry 1, against the valid set {1, 21, CHR_1, MT, chromosome, chr12} built at perl/Parser.t:117
have_chr - add chr: `_have_chr` returns 1 because the bare query 12 matches the prefixed valid entry chr12, against the valid set {1, 21, CHR_1, MT, chromosome, chr12} built at perl/Parser.t:117
have_chr - fail: `_have_chr` returns 0 because the contig 2, absent from the valid set, does not match, against the valid set {1, 21, CHR_1, MT, chromosome, chr12} built at perl/Parser.t:117
have_chr - M: a variant on chromosome M matches the valid set that contains MT, because _have_chr knows the two spellings are one contig
have_chr - convert M to MT: the match is not read-only -- _have_chr REWRITES the variant's chr from M to MT in place, so everything downstream sees the canonical spelling
load chr_synonyms: `chromosome_synonyms($file)` reads the synonyms TSV and returns true, so the alias table can be loaded at all
have_chr - synonym: the RefSeq accession NC_000021.9 matches the valid set through the loaded synonyms table, which no amount of chr-prefix juggling could achieve
chr unchanged after synonym check: matching through a synonym leaves the variant's chr as NC_000021.9, so the alias lookup matches without rewriting -- unlike the M to MT case

description: validate_vf - check_ref insertion: with check_ref on, an insertion (-/T over start 2, end 1) passes without a sequence comparison, because an insertion has no reference base to compare

validate_vf - lookup_ref insertion: an insertion (-/T over start 2, end 1) passes with lookup_ref on

basic next test: the six columns `21 25587759 25587759 C/A + test` parse to a VariationFeature with chr 21, start=end=25587759, strand 1, map_weight 1, allele_string C/A taken verbatim, variation_name `test` from the sixth column, and _line holding all six tokens
negative strand (-): the same row with `-` in the fifth column yields strand -1 and, notably, allele_string still C/A — the alleles are NOT reverse-complemented, only the strand flag changes
negative strand (-1): the numeric spelling `-1` in the fifth column produces exactly n=7's feature, so the two accepted spellings of the reverse strand are interchangeable

stubby: the four-column form `21 25587759 25587759 C/A`, with strand and id both omitted, parses to strand 1 and a *synthesised* variation_name `21_25587759_C/A` built from chromosome, start and allele string

SV dup: `21 25587759 25587769 DUP + test` parses to a StructuralVariationFeature — not a VariationFeature — with class_SO_term duplication and no allele_string or map_weight, the class switch being triggered by the allele column containing no `/`
SV inv: `21 25587759 25587769 INV + test` parses to a StructuralVariationFeature with class_SO_term inversion over the same span as n=10
SV del 1: the bare token `DEL` in the allele column parses to class_SO_term deletion — a symbolic deletion over an 11 bp span carrying no allele_string, unlike a sequence-level REF/- pair
SV del 2: the VCF-style angle-bracketed spelling `<DEL>` yields exactly n=12's StructuralVariationFeature, so the brackets are stripped rather than treated as part of the type name
SV CN0: the copy-number spelling `<CN0>` maps to class_SO_term deletion — zero copies is read as a loss, not as a generic copy-number event
SV CN2: `<CN2>` maps to class_SO_term duplication — two copies above the diploid baseline is read as a gain
SV CN3: `<CN3>` falls past both overrides to class_SO_term copy_number_variation — the generic case, and the last assertion of the format block
skip VF that fails validation: given `21 foo bar C/A 1` then a well-formed row, the first next() drops the line whose start and end are not numbers and returns the second, whose start is 25587759

dont skip VF that fails validation with dont_skip: with dont_skip => 1 the malformed row survives and its start comes back as the literal string `foo`, so the raw token is carried through unconverted rather than coerced or nulled
excerpt: is($vf->{start}, 'foo', 'dont skip VF that fails validation with dont_skip');

fetch after update 2: a third, disjoint [9, 10] insert stays separate, so a query spanning both returns the merged [1, 8] and [9, 10] as two intervals
load synonyms: the chromosome-synonyms file loads onto the tree and yields a truthy alias map
fetch - use synonyms: a RefSeq accession query (NC_000021.9) resolves through the synonyms map to chromosome 21
fetch - remove chr: a chr21 query reaches data stored under 21
fetch - add chr: a bare 21 query reaches data stored under chr21
insert and fetch object: a payload inserted with an interval comes back from a fetch carrying its own start and end
excerpt: is_deeply($t->fetch('chrobj', 7, 8), [{foo => 'bar', s => 5, e => 10}], 'insert and fetch object');

description: insert another doesn't merge: two payloads at overlapping coordinates both come back from one fetch
excerpt: is_deeply($t->fetch('chrobj', 7, 8), [{foo => 'bar', s => 5, e => 10}, {goo => 'car', s => 6, e => 12}], 'insert another doesn\'t merge');

description: _get_obj_start_end - arrayref: a payload given as [1, 5] yields start 1 and end 5
_get_obj_start_end - hashref 1: a payload given as {s, e} yields the same start and end as the arrayref form
_get_obj_start_end - hashref 2: the long field names {start, end} are accepted as well as the short {s, e}
_get_obj_start_end - no end: a payload carrying only a start is read as the single-base interval [start, start]
_get_obj_start_end throws no start: a payload with neither an s nor a start field dies with No start field
excerpt: throws_ok {$t->_get_obj_start_end({})} qr/No start field/, '_get_obj_start_end throws no start';

description: _get_dist arrayref 1: two disjoint intervals one base apart report distance 1
_get_dist arrayref 2: the measure is direction-blind, so a second interval lying before the first still reports 2
_get_dist arrayref overlap 0: intervals that share an endpoint report distance 0
_get_dist arrayref negative: negative coordinates go through the same absolute-difference arithmetic, giving 2
nearest - no result: querying a chromosome whose tree is empty returns an empty list rather than dying
nearest - left: a point between two intervals returns only the left one when it is nearer
nearest - right: the mirror case, where the right-hand interval is nearer, returns only that one
nearest - 2 hits: a point equidistant from both intervals returns both, not an arbitrary winner
excerpt: is_deeply($t->nearest('nearest', 8, 8), [{foo => 1, s => 1, e => 5}, {bar => 1, s => 11, e => 16}], 'nearest - 2 hits');

description: nearest - 2 hits input not length 1: distances are measured from the whole query interval, not from a single point, so a 7-9 query also ties
excerpt: is_deeply($t->nearest('nearest', 7, 9), [{foo => 1, s => 1, e => 5}, {bar => 1, s => 11, e => 16}], 'nearest - 2 hits input not length 1');

description: format_coords - same: a pair whose start equals its end renders as one bare number (1), never as the degenerate range 1-1
format_coords - diff 1: an ordered pair renders as start-end (1-2), joined by a single hyphen
format_coords - diff 2: a reversed pair (2, 1) is swapped and still renders as 1-2, never as 2-1
format_coords - missing 1: a known start with an unknown end renders as start-? (1-?), so the unknown bound prints as a question mark rather than being dropped
format_coords - missing 2: an unknown start with a known end renders as ?-end (?-1), the mirror image of the previous row
format_coords - missing 3: a pair with neither bound known renders as the single hyphen -
convert_arrayref - scalar: a lone scalar is returned unchanged, never given a separator
convert_arrayref - arrayref: an arrayref is flattened to a `,`-joined string (foo,bar)
convert_arrayref - arrayref with separator: an explicit separator replaces the default, giving foo&bar
numberify - arrayref: stringified numbers inside an arrayref become native numbers ('0','1' -> 0,1)
numberify - hashref: hash values are coerced too, including a fractional one ('0.1' -> 0.1)
numberify - mixed: coercion recurses into an arrayref sitting inside a hashref
numberify - float: '0.0001' becomes the number 0.0001 rather than staying a quoted string
numberify - exponential: '1e3' becomes 1000, so exponent notation is normalised away in the output
numberify - exempt keys intact: id and seq_region_name keep their string form even when they look numeric, so an all-digit identifier is never emitted unquoted
merge_hashes - simple: disjoint keys from both hashes survive the merge
merge_hashes - complex: the merge recurses into a nested hash and leaves an arrayref value intact
merge_hashes - complex inverted: swapping the two arguments produces the same merged hash
merge_hashes - overwrite: without the add flag the second hash's value replaces the first's
merge_hashes - add: with the add flag numeric values are summed (1 + 2 = 3) instead of replaced -- the arm the forked stats counters rely on
merge_hashes - array: array values are concatenated rather than one replacing the other
merge_arrays - simple: two disjoint arrays concatenate in argument order
merge_arrays - duplicates: an element already present in the first array is not appended a second time
merge_arrays - order: the first array's order is preserved and only the second's new elements are appended ([1,3] + [2,1,3,4] -> [1,3,2,4])
find_in_ref - simple: a wanted key at the top level yields its scalar wrapped in an arrayref
find_in_ref - two keys: every wanted key present is collected, each under its own name
find_in_ref - multiple values: walking a list of hashes accumulates both values under the one key
find_in_ref - multiple values in arrayref: an arrayref value contributes each of its scalars separately
find_in_ref - dont get non-scalars: hashes nested inside an arrayref are descended into and only their scalars are collected, never the hashrefs themselves
get_compressed_filehandle: a gzipped VCF opens and yields a readable handle
get_compressed_filehandle - no file: calling with no argument dies with `No file`, instead of returning an empty handle
get_compressed_filehandle - file does not exist: a nonexistent path dies with `File ... does not exist`
excerpt: throws_ok {get_compressed_filehandle('foobargoobar')} qr/File .+ does not exist/, 'get_compressed_filehandle - file does not exist';

description: get_compressed_filehandle - file not compressed: an uncompressed file handed to the gzip backend dies with `File ... binary` instead of being read as text
excerpt: throws_ok {get_compressed_filehandle($test_cfg->{test_vcf})} qr/File .+ binary/, 'get_compressed_filehandle - file not compressed';

description: get_compressed_filehandle - PerlIO::Gzip: with PerlIO::Gzip and gzip both installed the handle is a GLOB, i.e. the first backend in the chain served the open
get_compressed_filehandle - PerlIO::Gzip with multistream uses gzip: passing the multistream flag still yields a working handle, so concatenated gzip members are read through
get_compressed_filehandle - gzip: with PerlIO::Gzip disabled the handle is still a GLOB, i.e. the external gzip binary served the open
get_compressed_filehandle - IO::Uncompress::Gunzip: with PerlIO::Gzip and gzip both disabled the handle is an IO::Uncompress::Gunzip object, the third backend in the chain
get_compressed_filehandle - no available library: with all three backends disabled the call dies with `Cannot read from compressed or binary file`
excerpt: throws_ok {get_compressed_filehandle($test_cfg->{test_gzvcf})} qr/Cannot read from compressed or binary file/, 'get_compressed_filehandle - no available library';

description: get_time: the returned stamp matches YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS
get_version_data - ensembl-vep hashref: the ensembl-vep entry parses into a hash, so the tool's own version is structured like every other component's
get_version_data - ensembl-vep release: the parsed release field is numeric, so a version file that is not a number is a parse failure rather than a silently-quoted string
get_version_data - ensembl-vep sub: the parsed sub field is numeric on the same terms as release

get_version_data - the rest: the remaining components parse exactly -- ensembl at release 86 sub 0000001 and ensembl-variation at release 86 sub 0000000 -- so the zero-padded sub keeps its leading zeros
get_version_string: the rendered banner lists each component as `name : release.sub`, with ensembl-vep's own release and sub left free-form
BASIC TESTS: the VariantRecoder module loads under `use` -- the class that supplies this file's entire subject
new is defined: `VariantRecoder->new` with a live-DB config returns a defined object, i.e. the recoder accepts the DB-backed configuration this whole file runs under
set input_data: `param('input_data', 'rs142513484')` echoes the value it stored, so the recoder takes its input as a string through the config rather than from a file
check class: the object built two statements earlier is blessed into Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::VariantRecoder
init: `$vr->init()` reports success, i.e. the recoder's one-shot setup of parser and input buffer runs
init sets parser: after `init()` the recoder holds a parser object, so the string in input_data has been wrapped in an input source
init sets input_buffer: after `init()` the recoder also holds an input buffer, the second of the two objects its setup creates
reset deletes parser: `$vr->reset()` removes the parser that `init` created, so a recoder object can be re-driven with a new input
reset deletes input_buffer: `reset()` also removes the input buffer, so both objects n=6 and n=7 assert are torn down together
reset deletes input_data: `reset()` clears the config parameter itself, so the previous input string cannot be recoded twice by accident
recode - no input: calling `$vr->recode()` with input_data cleared dies with /No input data/ rather than returning an empty result
excerpt: throws_ok {$vr->recode()} qr/No input data/, 'recode - no input';

description: recode - <input>: for each of the 4 transcript-relative inputs (ENST00000352957.8:c.991G>A, NM_017446.3:c.991G>A, ENSP00000284967.6:p.Ala331Thr, NP_059142.2:p.Ala331Thr) the whole result structure is compared -- allele key A, and hgvsp/hgvsc/hgvsg/spdi/id/input lists naming all 3 proteins, all 5 transcripts, NC_000021.9:g.25585733C>T, NC_000021.9:25585732:C:T and rs142513484

recode - <input>: for each of the 3 already-genomic inputs (rs142513484, 21:g.25585733C>T, 21:25585732:C:T) the same full structure comes back, this time under allele key T -- so an rsID, genomic HGVS and SPDI all recode to the identical answer as the transcript inputs of n=12

recode - from gene gives multiple hgvsg: the gene-name input JAM2:c.721A>T yields three genomic notations (NC_000021.9:g.25706002A>T, g.25709954A>T, g.25712347A>T), one per transcript of the gene that carries a c.721
recode - limit fields: with `param('fields', ['hgvsg'])` the result carries only input and hgvsg, so --fields prunes the output structure rather than merely reordering it

recode - output vcf_string: with `fields => 'spdi', vcf_string => 1` the result carries a vcf_string of 21-25585733-C-T alongside the SPDI, i.e. the recoder can emit VCF coordinates as one more notation

recode - input HGVS and output vcf_string: the coding deletion ENST00000352957:c.971_973del becomes vcf_string 21-25585750-GTTA-G and spdi NC_000021.9:25585750:TTA:, so the anchor base VCF requires is added on output and SPDI's empty inserted field is kept

recode - insertion: rs1444184259 recodes to vcf_string 21-25639361-C-CC, spdi NC_000021.9:25639361::C and hgvsg NC_000021.9:g.25639361dup -- the same insertion rendered three ways, and HGVS prefers dup over ins
recode - input HGVS genomic insertion: 21:g.25639361_25639362insC produces the same three notations as n=18, so an insertion written as ins on input still comes back as dup on output
recode - output variant synonyms: with `var_synonyms => 1` the result gains a var_synonyms list carrying 'LSDB: NM_017446.3:c.991G>A', the identifier this variant has in an external database

recode - input hgvs, output variant synonyms: the same var_synonyms block is produced when the input is ENSP00000284967.6:p.Ala331Thr rather than an rsID, so synonym lookup happens after resolution and does not depend on the input notation

recode - output MANE Select: with `mane_select => 1` the result gains a mane_select list holding one hash of the MANE transcript's three notations (hgvsc ENST00000352957.8:c.991G>A, hgvsp ENSP00000284967.6:p.Ala331Thr, hgvsg NC_000021.9:g.25585733C>T)

recode - input synonyms variants (rs143054530), output MANE Select: driving the recoder from a file with `recode_all`, the first record's mane_select block is the ENST00000400075.3 / ENSP00000382948.3 / NC_000021.9:g.25764755G>A triple

recode - input synonyms variants (PA166153533), output MANE Select: the second record of the same file, whose identifier is a PharmGKB accession rather than an rsID, resolves to the identical mane_select triple as n=23
recode - output MANE Select and fields: with `mane_select => 1` and `fields => 'spdi'` the result keeps both the spdi list and the mane_select block, so mane_select is not one of the prunable fields

recode - SNV ID input - output GA4GH VRS Allele, SPDI: with `ga4gh_vrs => 1`, rs142513484 additionally yields a GA4GH VRS Allele object -- type Allele, a SequenceLocation on refseq:NC_000021.9 with a SimpleInterval 25585732-25585733, and a SequenceState of T

recode - SNV SPDI input - output GA4GH VRS Allele, SPDI: the same VRS Allele is produced when the input is the SPDI string NC_000021.9:25585732:C:T rather than the rsID, so VRS generation is independent of the input notation

recode - output MANE Select returns multiple genomic locations: the protein input GABPA:p.Trp189Ter gives a mane_select block whose sorted hgvsg values are NC_000021.9:g.25758022G>A and NC_000021.9:g.25758023G>A, so one MANE entry can carry more than one genomic position

recode - LRG input: LRG_485:6673:G:A recodes to hgvsg on both LRG_485 and the assembly (LRG_485:g.6674G>A and NC_000021.9:g.43774705C>T), plus LRG and Ensembl hgvsc and hgvsp, so LRG is a first-class reference system with a mapping to chr 21
the AnnotationSource::File base class loads under `use` -- outside the SKIP block, so it runs even where Bio::DB::HTS is missing
the AnnotationSource::File::GFF subclass loads under `use` -- the GFF transcript source the whole BAM-edit path hangs off
the Runner module loads under `use` before a runner is built to supply a config object
get new runner object: `Runner->new({base_testing_cfg, input_file => test_vcf})` returns a defined object, whose only use in this file is to hand its config to the GFF annotation source
new is defined: `AnnotationSource::File::GFF->new({file => bam_edit.gff, config})` returns a defined object, i.e. a GFF file is accepted as a transcript source
no bam provided: `$as->bam` is false on a GFF source constructed without one, so the BAM is optional and its absence is representable
apply_edits - no bam fails: `$as->apply_edits({})` returns false when no BAM is configured, so the edit step degrades to a no-op rather than dying
bam - no HTS installed: with $CAN_USE_HTS forced to 0, `$as->bam($file)` dies with /Cannot add BAM file/ rather than silently skipping the edits
excerpt: throws_ok {$as->bam($test_cfg->{bam_edit_bam})} qr/Cannot add BAM file/, 'bam - no HTS installed';

description: bam - give filename: `$as->bam($file)` given a path returns a Bio::DB::HTS handle, i.e. the accessor opens the alignment rather than just storing the string
bam - give filename at new(): passing `bam => $file` to the constructor gives the same Bio::DB::HTS handle as the setter of n=9, so the two configuration routes converge
setup fasta_db: the GFF source lazily opens a FASTA sequence database, because a GFF carries annotation but no sequence and the edits cannot be checked without one
load synonyms: `$as->chromosome_synonyms($file)` loads the chromosome-name synonym table, which is what lets a GFF and BAM named NC_000021.9 line up with a VCF named 21
get transcripts: lazily loading every transcript the GFF yields over regions 10 to 46 of NC_000021.9 gives exactly 35, the set every later row edits
apply_edits - _bam_edit_status already set: `apply_edits` on a transcript that already carries `_bam_edit_status` returns true without redoing the work, so the step is idempotent
apply_edits: the first real call, on transcript 0 of the 35, returns true -- the alignment was found and the edits were applied
apply_edits - spliced_seq: after the edits, transcript 0's spliced sequence equals a specific 2.7 kb string, so the corrections are actually written into the sequence and not merely recorded

apply_edits - edit attribs: the edits are recorded as two _rna_edit attributes, '256 256 A' and '1547 1547 G', each described as 'Edit from bam_edit.bam, op=X len=1 mapped to <range>', so the provenance and the CIGAR op are kept
apply_edits - _bam_edit_status: after a successful edit the transcript is marked `_bam_edit_status = ok`, the marker n=14 short-circuits on and n=30 contrasts with
NM_001286476.1 - get: the named RefSeq transcript is present among the 35 of n=13, so the later assertions address a specific transcript rather than whichever happened to sort first
NM_001286476.1 - apply_edits: the edit replay succeeds on this second transcript too, setting up the insertion-heavy attribute comparison of n=21

NM_001286476.1 - apply_edits - edit attribs: four insertion edits are recorded, op=I of lengths 13, 1, 1 and 1 at mapped ranges 2966-2965, 2941-2940, 2618-2617 and 920-919 -- note each is an empty range, which is how an insertion is expressed
apply_edits - check all: running the edit over all 35 transcripts leaves all 35 with `_bam_edit_status = ok`, so the replay succeeds on the whole GFF set and not only on the two inspected transcripts
NM_032195.2 - get: the third named transcript, chosen because its alignment contains a soft-clip, is present among the 35
NM_032195.2 - apply_edits: the replay succeeds on the soft-clipped alignment rather than refusing it

NM_032195.2 - apply edits - edit attribs - include S: two edits are recorded, op=X len=1 at 3660-3660 and op=S len=16 at 7504-7503, so soft-clipped bases are turned into an edit instead of being discarded

apply_edits - rseq_mrna_match returns ok: a transcript already carrying an `rseq_mrna_match` attribute is returned successfully without being edited, because Ensembl has already certified that its sequence matches the RefSeq mRNA
apply_edits - rseq_mrna_match no _bam_edit_status: the skipped transcript of n=26 is left with no `_bam_edit_status` at all, so a skip is distinguishable from a success

apply_edits - sequences match anyway: with the certificate attribute removed, the same transcript still returns success, because the comparison finds the sequences identical and simply records no edits

fail - NM_001286476.1 - apply_edits returns undef: after one exon base is corrupted to N, the replay returns undef instead of writing edits, so a sequence that cannot be reconciled is refused rather than patched
fail - NM_001286476.1 - _bam_edit_status failed: the refused transcript is marked `_bam_edit_status = failed`, the value that later suppresses HGVS output for it
fail - NM_001286476.1 - no edit attribs: a failed transcript is left with zero attributes, so a partially applied edit set is never exposed
fail - no alignment: a transcript whose stable id was changed to 'foo', so that the BAM contains no read group for it, makes `apply_edits` return undef
release self-check, step 1: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` in the checkout yields a non-empty branch name — the value rows 2 and 3 are compared against
ensembl-vep version data: `get_version_data()` yields a per-module record (a HASH) for `ensembl-vep` — the structure the `##VEP=` VCF header is formatted from
ensembl-vep release matches git release: the compiled-in `$VEP_VERSION` (116) equals the NN captured from the `release/NN` branch name
